_job: Job 2: FIANZ Ramadhan Calendar 1447H (fianz.com successor sheets) — angle pair behind the stated-offset sheet
_engine: adhan 4.4.6, second resolution, explicit nearest-minute rounding, no real clock

window.note: Ramadan window only — the pair is fitted inside it and extrapolation outside it is not tested by this surface

statedOffsetsVerbatim.suhoor: 5 minutes allowed between end of Suhur and Fajr
statedOffsetsVerbatim.iftar: 5 minutes allowed between sunset and Iftar/Maghrib
statedOffsetsVerbatim.asr: single shadow primary; double shadow +40 min

statedOffsetsCheck.suhoorEnds_equals_fajr_minus_5: EXACT in all 90 rows across the three cities (sd 0)
statedOffsetsCheck.magrib_equals_sunset_plus_5: holds to minute rounding at Auckland and Christchurch (median +5.3/+5.6, sd 0.29); Wellington reads +4.0 — see coordinate note
statedOffsetsCheck.asr_single_shadow: confirmed: shadow-1 residuals ~0 (+0.2..+0.7), shadow-2 residual ~ -55 min

verdict.detail: Implied-angle clusters are tight (sd ~0.05-0.06 deg): Auckland fajr 18.08 / isha 17.96 -> 18/18; Wellington fajr 16.14 / isha 15.08 -> 16/15; Christchurch fajr 16.07 / isha 14.99 -> 16/15. The federation sheet is per-city calculated, and the North Island city runs the standard 18/18 while the two southern sheets run 16/15.
verdict.wellingtonCoordinateNote: Wellington solar columns sit early vs the census coordinates (sunrise -4.3 min, dhuhr -1.5 min) while Auckland/Christchurch sit on ~0 — the Wellington sheet was likely computed for a slightly different grid point; the angle clusters are insensitive to this (~0.02 deg).
verdict.stability: Single Ramadan window on the surface; between-year stability not testable. Within-window residuals are flat (no drift across the 30 days).
limits: Ramadan 1447H window only (30 rows/city): fajr and isha angles are fitted inside a late-summer New Zealand window; high-latitude extrapolation outside it (especially winter twilight behaviour) is not vouched for.
Sheet Ramadan 1 = 2026-02-19 while FIANZ Hilal confirmation printed 2026-02-20 (two-editions pattern, recorded at capture time).
